messages:
opsbot: INCIDENT ALERT: elevated 5xx rate and latency in eu-west region detected (metric spike at ~06:12 UTC). Automated correlation suggests upstream transit provider CarrierZ (ASN 64500) — paging #incidents and on-call.
pagerduty-bot: Paging maya (net-oncall) — escalation level: P1. Acknowledge in channel to stop repeat pages.
maya: ack. seeing ~30% increase in 5xx across eu-west-apiserver pool. digging into egress traces now. traceroutes from edge-euw-1 show intermittent packet loss starting at 203.0.113.1 (CarrierZ) then recovered, repeated.
jordan: noticing BGP churn to ASN 64500 around same window. pulling bgp neighbor summary for our egress pair.
jordan: ```
# show ip bgp neighbors 203.0.113.1
BGP neighbor is 203.0.113.1, remote AS 64500, neighbor is up
  Last read 00:00:12, hold time is 180, keepalive 60 sec
  Received 12 prefixes, 1 path changes, 3 notifications
  Session flaps: 5 in last 20m
Interface errors: ifInErrors high on eth1/3 toward 203.0.113.1
```
eli: if the carrier is flapping, we should shift pref path to backup provider Y. Options: 1) prepend to CarrierZ to discourage selection, 2) announce more-specifics via BackupY, 3) use BGP community to influence upstream peers. I can push changes to route policy if we decide.
sam: quick note — announcing more-specifics may increase churn at our routers; also watch for RPKI/filters. If we do prepends, do it in small batches and monitor edge CPU.
maya: opened ticket with CarrierZ NOC (#987654). they responded: "we're seeing interface errors and are investigating". asked for ETA and whether they have unilateral mitigation.
nisha: support check-in — customers on eu-west region are seeing partial request failures; top impacted product is streaming inference sessions (resets). I have a list of high-traffic customers and alerted account teams.
opsbot: INCIDENT: severity -> P1, status: investigating. Incident channel pinned; set retrospective reminder.
jordan: proposed immediate mitigation: add 3x AS-PREPEND to routes advertised to CarrierZ and announce high-priority /24s via BackupY, then withdraw if stable. I'll stage the change in config and run a canary push.
eli: I'll take the config push. plan: 1) apply prepend-only route-map toward CarrierZ; 2) announce additional /24s to BackupY; 3) monitor BGP paths and application errors. ETA 10m for first change.
maya: go for it. communicate start/complete in-channel. also updating status page draft: "Some EU traffic experiencing elevated errors; rerouting in progress."
jordan: starting staged push now — applying route-map as described.
jordan: ```
# bgp config snippet
route-map PREPEND_TO_CARRIER permit 10
  set as-path prepend 64500 64500 64500
neighbor 203.0.113.1 route-map PREPEND_TO_CARRIER out
```
jordan: change applied to egress-edge-euw-1 and egress-edge-euw-2. monitoring.
maya: metrics: within 6 minutes, 5xx rate dropped from 30% over baseline to ~8% above baseline. traceroutes show majority of traffic now preferring BackupY path (198.51.100.2).
opsbot: SYSTEM NOTE: anomaly detectors still flagged small bursts but trend is down. continue monitoring for 30m before declaring mitigated.
sam: FYI — edge CPU on egress-edge-euw-1 jumped 12% during reroute but within safe limits. no route flaps observed on BackupY session.
nisha: customer update drafted and sent to critical accounts. posting public status announced under "service degraded" for eu-west with notes about reroute.
maya: CarrierZ NOC replied: "we see interface errors and scheduled maintenance on affected fiber segment, have high-priority ticket in carrier queue." they will confirm post-maintenance behavior. asked them to provide root cause and expected full restoration window.
jordan: starting logs/pcap collection on border interfaces for postmortem. saving bgp dump (bgpdump) at 06:30 UTC and exporting to incident artifacts.
eli: incoming handoff — I will take primary on-call at 07:30 UTC. plan to keep prepends in place for 2 hours and then evaluate if we should withdraw or keep as long-term if carrier intermittent. also propose adding a transient routing policy to prefer BackupY for eu-west for production prefixes until carrier confirms fix.
maya: handoff notes: actions taken, ticket #987654 with CarrierZ, prepends applied, BackupY announcement active, customer impact reduced, artifacts collected, support notified.
pagerduty-bot: Handoff accepted by eli. Next on-call: eli (netops). Escalation policy remains P1 if error rate >15% for 10m.
eli: acknowledged. will keep monitoring and update status if behavior changes. creating follow-up runbook items: collect BGP history, check RPKI impact, and verify no collateral routing changes for other regions.
maya: thx team. I'll create a brief incident entry and schedule postmortem once we stabilize. closing initial mitigation loop — incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. will update when CarrierZ confirms full restoration or if we see regression. :white_check_mark:
